summary: Interlude (S3 US-East-1, 2017) answered. The story's core: a circular dependency made the health system fail exactly when needed -- the dashboard stored assets in S3, so it could not report S3 down; and every remediation changed the SYSTEM, not the person. Applied to the fork: (1) Circular dependencies -- audit: the app's /health and /ready endpoints only check the API process and Redis connectivity; the click pipeline (redirect -> Redis broker -> Celery worker -> Postgres) is the fork's dependency chain, and its monitoring gap is that /ready does NOT check the queue: if Redis is up but the worker is dead, redirects still 302 (clicks enqueue fine) but analytics silently stall -- the system that reports analytics health (the analytics endpoint) depends on the very worker that processes clicks. That is a latent S3-style circular dependency: analytics aggregator reads Postgres, which depends on the worker, which depends on the broker. (2) Guardrails audit -- the fork's dangerous single-command surface: links_service delete_link is a hard DELETE with no confirmation or dry-run, and no transaction guard prevents deleting an entire user's links in one call (DELETE /links/{id} is scoped by owner, but there is no bulk-delete cap); the S3 lesson maps to 'no sanity check on a destructive operation'. Also the create_link code is generated (62^6) so no human-parameter danger there. (3) Postmortem standard: every remediation in the S3 report changes structure, not people -- for the fork's M6 cache invalidation regression I already applied this: the namespace-ownership documentation and DB-level dedup are structural (the bug cannot recur even if a future engineer forgets), rather than 'be more careful with cache keys'. Holding to this standard for M7.
evidence: Fork health-check audit: /ready does not verify queue/worker liveness (circular dependency class)
Guardrail audit: hard delete with no confirmation/cap is the fork's S3-parallel dangerous surface
M6 fix already structural (dedup in DB unique constraint, not human discipline)
